title: A Novel Proposal: Glycosylated Dendritic Nanoparticles for Targeted Delivery of Genetic Payload to Cancer Cells
content: This communication proposes a new monomer that will self-assemble into a cancer-targeting glycosylated dendritic nanoparticle (DNP). This combines previously developed DNP technology used for genetic payload delivery (Ionizable Amphiphilic Janus Dendrimers or IAJDs) with experimentation on glycosylated PAMAM dendrimers’ interactions with cancer cells. The combined result is a DNP that can target cancer cells for delivery of genetic payload. To demonstrate feasibility, a rough approximation of synthetic pathway, adjustment to the self-assembly mechanism, and possible improvements to payload retention are described. This work represents a hypothesis-driven synthetic proposal rather than a validated result, intended to motivate experimental testing of a combined targeting-and-delivery dendrimer platform for cancer-directed gene therapies.
